I.explanation: "I" means "you" when you talk to two or more people. Compare Du er min ven (You are my friend, one person) with I er mine venner (You are my friends, a group). It is not jeg (I), and it is not the small word i (in): I bor i Aarhus (You live in Aarhus).

related.en: you (group), as in "Jeg ser jer" (I see you)

sentence.da: **I** er mine venner.
sentence.en: You are all my friends.

at iagttage.explanation: "At iagttage" means "to observe": to watch something carefully, on purpose and over some time, to learn about it, such as animals, weather or people. Unlike at se (to see), it needs attention.

sentence.da: Forskeren vil **iagttage** ulvene i flere uger og skrive noter.
sentence.en: The researcher wants to observe the wolves for several weeks and write notes.

at identificere.explanation: "At identificere" means "to identify", to work out exactly who or what someone or something is. To prove who you are, add sig: Jeg skal identificere mig (I have to identify myself).

sentence.da: Politiet kan **identificere** manden på billedet.
sentence.en: The police can identify the man in the picture.

at igangsætte.explanation: "At igangsætte" means "to initiate": to get a project, a process or an investigation going. It belongs to official and business language: Ministeriet igangsætter en undersøgelse (The ministry is starting a study). In everyday talk, at starte (to start) is more usual.

sentence.da: Kommunen vil **igangsætte** byggeriet af den nye skole.
sentence.en: The city wants to start the construction of the new school.

at ignorere.explanation: "At ignorere" means "to ignore", to pay no attention to something on purpose. It is used for people and also for things like rules, warnings and messages: Han ignorerer alle beskeder (He ignores all messages).

sentence.da: Du må ikke **ignorere** en advarsel fra lægen.
sentence.en: You must not ignore a warning from the doctor.

at illustrere.explanation: "At illustrere" means "to illustrate", in two ways: to add pictures to a book, and to make something clear with an example: Det illustrerer problemet (That makes the problem clear).

sentence.da: Hun vil **illustrere** børnebogen med farverige tegninger.
sentence.en: She wants to illustrate the children's book with colorful drawings.

at implementere.explanation: "At implementere" means "to implement", to put a plan, a rule or a computer system into real use. It is about acting on what was already decided: Firmaet implementerer det nye system i dag (The company is implementing the new system today).

sentence.da: Skolen vil **implementere** de nye regler næste måned.
sentence.en: The school will implement the new rules next month.

at imponere.explanation: "At imponere" means "to impress": Hendes tale imponerede os (Her speech impressed us). To say someone is impressed, use imponeret: Jeg er imponeret (I am impressed).

sentence.da: Han vil **imponere** sin chef med en god idé.
sentence.en: He wants to impress his boss with a good idea.

at importere.explanation: "At importere" means "to import", to bring goods into a country from abroad. It also means to bring files into a computer program. The opposite, for goods going out, is at eksportere (to export).

sentence.da: Vi må **importere** bananer, fordi de ikke vokser i Danmark.
sentence.en: We must import bananas because they do not grow in Denmark.

at indbyde.explanation: "At indbyde" means "to invite", in a more formal way than at invitere (to invite). It is used in writing and speeches, for example in an announcement: Vi indbyder til generalforsamling (We invite you to the general meeting).

sentence.da: Skolen vil **indbyde** alle forældre til et møde.
sentence.en: The school wants to invite all parents to a meeting.

at inddrage.explanation: "At inddrage" means "to involve", to bring someone into a decision or a discussion: Vi vil inddrage børnene i beslutningen (We want to involve the children in the decision). It can also mean to remove something officially: inddrage et kørekort (to revoke a driver's license).

sentence.da: Læreren vil **inddrage** eleverne, når klassen planlægger turen.
sentence.en: The teacher wants to involve the students when the class plans the trip.

at indebære.explanation: "At indebære" means "to involve" or "to imply", and says what something necessarily brings with it. It is used about things like a job, a plan or a change, not about people: Ændringen indebærer flere udgifter (The change involves higher costs).

sentence.da: Mit nye job vil **indebære** mange rejser.
sentence.en: My new job will involve many trips.

at indeholde.explanation: "At indeholde" means "to contain": Saften indeholder meget sukker (The juice contains a lot of sugar).

sentence.da: Pas på, kagen kan **indeholde** nødder.
sentence.en: Careful, the cake may contain nuts.

at indfri.explanation: "At indfri" means "to fulfill". It is used for what was promised or hoped for: indfri et løfte (fulfill a promise), indfri forventninger (live up to expectations). With money it means to settle a debt in full: indfri et lån (settle a loan).

sentence.da: Hun vil **indfri** sin drøm og blive læge.
sentence.en: She wants to fulfill her dream and become a doctor.

at indføre.explanation: "At indføre" means "to introduce (a rule)", to start a new law, rule or system for everyone: Kommunen indfører nye regler (The municipality is introducing new rules). To introduce people to each other, use at præsentere (to present).

sentence.da: Regeringen vil **indføre** en ny skat på sukker.
sentence.en: The government wants to introduce a new tax on sugar.

at indgive.explanation: "At indgive" means "to submit" or "to file" an official paper to an authority, such as a court or a city office: indgive en ansøgning (submit an application). It sounds official, so it fits papers and forms, not everyday things.

sentence.da: Jeg vil **indgive** en klage til kommunen, fordi gaden er farlig.
sentence.en: I will file a complaint with the city because the street is dangerous.

at indgå.explanation: "At indgå" means "to enter into", mainly an agreement, a deal or a marriage: indgå ægteskab (get married). With i after it, it means "to be part of": Mel indgår i opskriften (Flour is part of the recipe).

sentence.da: De to lande vil **indgå** en aftale om fred.
sentence.en: The two countries want to make an agreement on peace.

at indhente.explanation: "At indhente" means "to catch up with" someone or something that is ahead of you. It also means to make up for lost time: indhente det forsømte (make up for what was missed). In formal use it means to get information or offers from others: indhente tilbud (get quotes).

sentence.da: Hun løb hurtigt for at **indhente** de andre.
sentence.en: She ran fast to catch up with the others.

at indikere.explanation: "At indikere" means "to indicate", to be a clue about something or to point toward it: Resultaterne indikerer, at planen virker (The results indicate that the plan works).

sentence.da: Røg kan **indikere**, at der er ild.
sentence.en: Smoke can indicate that there is fire.

at indkalde.explanation: "At indkalde" means "to call in" or "to summon", to officially order people to come: Retten indkalder vidner (The court summons witnesses). It is also used for a meeting that someone formally calls.

sentence.da: Bestyrelsen vil **indkalde** medlemmerne til et møde.
sentence.en: The board wants to call the members to a meeting.

at indkøbe.explanation: "At indkøbe" means "to purchase", to buy goods for a company, an office or a shop: Firmaet indkøber nye stole (The company is purchasing new chairs). For everyday food shopping, Danes say at købe ind (to do the shopping).

sentence.da: Kommunen vil **indkøbe** nye computere til skolerne.
sentence.en: The municipality wants to purchase new computers for the schools.

at indlede.explanation: "At indlede" means "to begin" or "to introduce", used for the first step of something with several parts, such as a speech, a negotiation or a relationship: indlede et forhold (begin a relationship).

sentence.da: Præsidenten vil **indlede** mødet med en kort tale.
sentence.en: The president wants to begin the meeting with a short speech.

at indrette.explanation: "At indrette" means "to furnish" or "to set up" a room, a home or a shop, so that everything has its place: Jeg indretter et kontor (I am setting up an office).

sentence.da: Hun vil **indrette** soveværelset med et stort skab.
sentence.en: She wants to furnish the bedroom with a big wardrobe.

at indrette sig.explanation: "At indrette sig" means "to settle in" and to arrange your life to fit a new situation: Vi har indrettet os i en lille lejlighed (We have settled into a small apartment). Without sig, at indrette means to furnish a room: indrette et værelse (furnish a room).

sentence.da: Når man flytter til udlandet, må man **indrette sig** efter nye regler.
sentence.en: When you move abroad, you have to adapt to new rules.

at indrømme.explanation: "At indrømme" means "to admit", to say that something is true, often something unpleasant like a mistake: Jeg indrømmer, at jeg tog fejl (I admit that I was wrong).

sentence.da: Han ville ikke **indrømme**, at han havde glemt det.
sentence.en: He did not want to admit that he had forgotten it.

at indsamle.explanation: "At indsamle" means "to collect", to gather things from many sources, such as money, data or old clothes. For a hobby, use at samle (to collect): Jeg samler på frimærker (I collect stamps).

sentence.da: Vi vil **indsamle** penge til de syge børn.
sentence.en: We want to collect money for the sick children.

at indse.explanation: "At indse" means "to realize", when you see something you missed before: Jeg indså for sent, at det var en fejl (I realized too late that it was a mistake).

sentence.da: Du må **indse**, at han har ret.
sentence.en: You have to realize that he is right.

at indsende.explanation: "At indsende" means "to submit", to send something to an office, a company or a competition so that it can be looked at: indsende en ansøgning (submit an application).

sentence.da: Du skal **indsende** skemaet før fredag.
sentence.en: You must submit the form before Friday.

at indskrænke.explanation: "At indskrænke" means "to restrict": to make the space for something smaller. It is used for money, freedom and activity: indskrænke forbruget (cut down use), indskrænke friheden (curb freedom).

sentence.da: Kommunen vil **indskrænke** åbningstiden i weekenden.
sentence.en: The city wants to restrict the opening hours on the weekend.

at indstille.explanation: "At indstille" means "to set" or "to adjust" a device so it works as you want: indstille uret (set the clock). It also means to put forward someone for a prize or a job: indstille en kandidat (recommend a candidate).

sentence.da: Du kan **indstille** vækkeuret til klokken syv.
sentence.en: You can set the alarm clock to seven o'clock.

at indstille sig på.explanation: "At indstille sig på" means "to prepare for" something you know is coming: Vi må indstille os på en kold vinter (We must prepare for a cold winter). It also means to accept that things will be different: Jeg har indstillet mig på at flytte (I have accepted that I will move).

forms.en: I have prepared for / adjusted to

sentence.da: Man må **indstille sig på** lange køer i ferien.
sentence.en: You have to get ready for long lines during vacation.

at indsætte.explanation: "At indsætte" means "to insert" something into a place, and also "to deposit" money: indsætte penge (deposit money). The opposite for money is at hæve (to withdraw).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **indsætte** pengene, før banken lukker.
sentence.en: I want to deposit the money before the bank closes.

at indtage.explanation: "At indtage" means "to consume" food or medicine, and is used on labels and in instructions: Medicinen skal indtages med vand (The medicine must be taken with water). It also means to capture a place: Soldaterne indtog byen (The soldiers captured the town).

sentence.da: Man må ikke **indtage** alkohol, når man kører bil.
sentence.en: You must not consume alcohol when you drive.

at informere.explanation: "At informere" means "to inform", telling someone the facts: Skolen informerer forældrene (The school informs the parents). To say what about, add om: Jeg informerer dig om det (I am informing you about it).

sentence.da: Vi vil **informere** alle om ændringen i morgen.
sentence.en: We will inform everyone about the change tomorrow.

at insistere.explanation: "At insistere" means "to insist", to keep saying that something must happen. After it, use på (on): Hun insisterer på at gå hjem (She insists on going home).

sentence.da: Han vil **insistere** på at betale regningen.
sentence.en: He will insist on paying the bill.

at inspirere.explanation: "At inspirere" means "to inspire", to give someone new ideas or the wish to do something. The source can be a person, a book or a place: Rejser inspirerer mig (Travel inspires me).

sentence.da: Gode bøger kan **inspirere** børn til at skrive selv.
sentence.en: Good books can inspire children to write themselves.

at installere.explanation: "At installere" means "to install", to put a program on a computer or phone so it works: Jeg installerer en ny app (I install a new app).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **installere** et nyt program i dag.
sentence.en: I have to install a new program today.

at integrere.explanation: "At integrere" means "to integrate", to make someone or something a full part of a group or a whole. It is common about newcomers in a society: at integrere flygtninge (to integrate refugees).

sentence.da: Skolen vil **integrere** de nye elever i klassen.
sentence.en: The school wants to integrate the new students into the class.

at intensivere.explanation: "At intensivere" means "to intensify", to make something more forceful or more active: Politiet intensiverer eftersøgningen (The police are intensifying the search). It also fits efforts, training and campaigns.

sentence.da: Holdet vil **intensivere** træningen før den store kamp.
sentence.en: The team wants to intensify the training before the big match.

at interessere.explanation: "At interessere" means "to interest", and the thing that interests you comes first: Fodbold interesserer mig (Soccer interests me). To say you are interested, use Jeg er interesseret i fodbold (I am interested in soccer).

sentence.da: Den bog kan **interessere** dig.
sentence.en: That book might interest you.

at interessere sig for.explanation: "At interessere sig for" means "to be interested in": Jeg interesserer mig for musik (I am interested in music). The little word changes with the person: mig for I, dig for you, sig for he or she: Hun interesserer sig for kunst (She is interested in art).

sentence.da: Små børn kan **interessere sig for** dyr og biler.
sentence.en: Small children can be interested in animals and cars.

at interviewe.explanation: "At interviewe" means "to interview", to ask someone questions for a news story, a study or a job: Journalisten interviewer ministeren (The journalist is interviewing the minister).

sentence.da: Hun vil **interviewe** tre kandidater til jobbet i dag.
sentence.en: She wants to interview three candidates for the job today.

at introducere.explanation: "At introducere" means "to introduce", bringing in something new: Hun introducerer en ny metode (She introduces a new method). For introducing a person, at præsentere (to present) is more common: Må jeg præsentere Anna? (May I introduce Anna?)

sentence.da: Skolen vil **introducere** et nyt fag næste år.
sentence.en: The school will introduce a new subject next year.

at invadere.explanation: "At invadere" means "to invade", to enter a country with an army by force. It is also used when a place is filled by many people or animals: Turisterne invaderer byen (The tourists are invading the town).

sentence.da: Når en hær vil **invadere** et land, kommer den over grænsen.
sentence.en: When an army wants to invade a country, it crosses the border.

at investere.explanation: "At investere" means "to invest", to put money into something in order to earn more later, such as a company or a house. It also works for time and effort: Jeg investerer mange timer i projektet (I invest many hours in the project).

sentence.da: Hun vil **investere** sine penge i en lille butik.
sentence.en: She wants to invest her money in a small shop.

at invitere.explanation: "At invitere" means "to invite". Jeg inviterer dig til min fødselsdag means "I invite you to my birthday". Til (to) goes before the event you invite someone to.

sentence.da: Jeg vil **invitere** mine venner til middag.
sentence.en: I want to invite my friends to dinner.

at irritere.explanation: "At irritere" means "to irritate" and "to annoy": Larmen irriterer mig (The noise annoys me). To say you are annoyed, use Jeg er irriteret (I am annoyed).

sentence.da: Det kan **irritere** mig, når du kommer for sent.
sentence.en: It can annoy me when you arrive late.

at isolere.explanation: "At isolere" means "to isolate", to keep something apart, and also "to insulate" a building against cold or noise: Vi isolerer loftet (We are insulating the attic).

sentence.da: Vi vil **isolere** væggene, fordi huset er koldt om vinteren.
sentence.en: We want to insulate the walls because the house is cold in winter.

en iagttager.explanation: "En iagttager" means "an observer", someone who watches something carefully without taking part in it. It can be a person who studies animals or a person who follows events and reports on them.

sentence.da: En god **iagttager** ser små ting, som andre ikke lægger mærke til.
sentence.en: A good observer sees small things that others do not notice.

en identitet.explanation: "En identitet" means "an identity", who a person is or feels they are, such as their background and values. A group, a country or a company can have an identitet too, for example the look and feel that makes it recognizable.

sentence.da: Hendes sprog og hendes familie er en stor del af hendes **identitet**.
sentence.en: Her language and her family are a big part of her identity.

en idrætshal.explanation: "En idrætshal" means "a sports hall", a big indoor building for sports like handball, badminton and gymnastics. Most Danish towns have one, and local clubs use it for training in the evening.

sentence.da: Børnene spiller håndbold og badminton i den store **idrætshal**.
sentence.en: The children play handball and badminton in the big sports hall.

en idé.explanation: "En idé" means "an idea", a thought about what to do or a way to solve something. Det er en god idé means "That is a good idea", and Jeg har ingen idé means "I have no idea".

sentence.da: Har du en **idé** til aftensmad?
sentence.en: Do you have an idea for dinner?

en igangsætter.explanation: "En igangsætter" means "an initiator", a person who gets a project, an idea or a change started. It comes from at sætte i gang (to set something going). It is about the starting push, not about running the whole thing afterward.

sentence.da: Hun var **igangsætter** på projektet, og alle andre fulgte med.
sentence.en: She was the initiator of the project, and everyone else followed.

en illusion.explanation: "En illusion" means "an illusion", something that looks real but is not. It is used for tricks of the eye and also for false hopes: Jeg har ingen illusioner om det (I have no illusions about it) means you are realistic about it.

sentence.da: Spejlene på væggen skaber en **illusion** af et større rum.
sentence.en: The mirrors on the wall create an illusion of a bigger room.

en illustration.explanation: "En illustration" means "an illustration", a picture that goes with a text and helps explain it, as in a book or a magazine. It can also mean an example that makes a point clear.

sentence.da: Den lille **illustration** ved siden af teksten viser, hvordan maskinen virker.
sentence.en: The small illustration next to the text shows how the machine works.

en implikation.explanation: "En implikation" means "an implication", something that follows from a decision or a fact without being said directly. It is often used in the plural: Hvad er implikationerne? (What are the implications?)

sentence.da: Politikerne diskuterer den økonomiske **implikation** af den nye lov.
sentence.en: The politicians discuss the economic implication of the new law.

en indbakke.explanation: "En indbakke" means "an inbox", the place where new messages arrive. It is built from ind (in) and bakke (tray). Bakke also means a hill: Cyklen ruller ned ad bakken (The bike rolls down the hill).

sentence.da: Jeg tjekker min **indbakke** hver morgen.
sentence.en: I check my inbox every morning.

en indblanding.explanation: "En indblanding" means "an interference", when someone gets involved in something that is not their business. It is almost always negative: Hun bryder sig ikke om andres indblanding (She does not like other people butting in).

sentence.da: Politikerne kritiserede statens **indblanding** i skolen.
sentence.en: The politicians criticized the state's interference in the school.

en indbygger.explanation: "En indbygger" means "an inhabitant", a person who lives in a town, a city or a country.

sentence.da: En **indbygger** bor i en by eller et land.
sentence.en: An inhabitant lives in a town or a country.

en inddragelse.explanation: "En inddragelse" means "an involvement", bringing people in so they can take part in a decision: inddragelse af borgerne (involving the residents). It is not the same as indblanding (interference), which people do not want. The same word also means taking something away officially: inddragelse af kørekort (taking away a driver's license).

sentence.da: Forældrenes **inddragelse** gør, at skolen hører, hvad de mener.
sentence.en: The parents' involvement means the school hears what they think.

en inder.explanation: "En inder" means "an Indian", a person from India. Do not mix it up with en indianer (a Native American), which looks almost the same. The country is Indien (India), and food or music from there is called indisk (Indian).

sentence.da: Min kollega er **inder** og kommer fra byen Mumbai.
sentence.en: My colleague is Indian and comes from the city of Mumbai.

en inderside.explanation: "En inderside" means "an inside", the inner surface of something. It is built from inder (inner) and side (side). Side also means a page: side 12 (page 12).

sentence.da: Der står et navn på jakkens **inderside**.
sentence.en: There is a name on the inside of the jacket.

en indflydelse.explanation: "En indflydelse" means "an influence", the power to affect what other people think or do. The usual phrase is at have indflydelse på (to have influence on): Jeg har ingen indflydelse på det (I have no say in it).

sentence.da: Forældrene har stor **indflydelse** på, hvad børnene tror på.
sentence.en: The parents have a big influence on what the children believe.

en indflytning.explanation: "En indflytning" means "a move-in", the act or day of moving into a new home. Indflytning er den første maj (Move-in is on the first of May) is a typical way to give the date. The part ind (in) shows the direction, and it is the same part as in indgang (entrance).

sentence.da: Ved **indflytning** skal du tage billeder af lejlighedens stand.
sentence.en: At move-in you must take pictures of the apartment's condition.

en indflytningsgave.explanation: "En indflytningsgave" means "a housewarming gift", a present you give to people who have just moved into a new home. It is built from indflytning (moving in) and gave (gift). Gave also appears in en julegave (a Christmas present).

sentence.da: Vi giver dem en **indflytningsgave**, når de flytter ind.
sentence.en: We give them a housewarming gift when they move in.

en indfødsretsprøve.explanation: "En indfødsretsprøve" means "a citizenship test", the test about Danish society, history and culture that you must pass to apply for Danish nationality. It is built from indfødsret (the right of a native) and prøve (test).

sentence.da: Man skal bestå en **indfødsretsprøve** for at blive dansk statsborger.
sentence.en: You must pass a citizenship test to become a Danish citizen.

en indgang.explanation: "En indgang" means "an entrance", the place where you go in, such as the door of a building or the gate of a park. It is built from ind (in) and gang (passage). Gang also means a hallway: Skoene står i gangen (The shoes are in the hallway).

sentence.da: Man går ind gennem en **indgang** og ud gennem en udgang.
sentence.en: You go in through an entrance and out through an exit.

en indkaldelse.explanation: "En indkaldelse" means "a summons / notice", an official message that calls you to show up. It is used for meetings, hospital appointments and military service: indkaldelse til generalforsamling (notice of a general meeting).

sentence.da: Jeg har fået en **indkaldelse** til et møde på mandag.
sentence.en: I have received a notice for a meeting on Monday.

en indkomst.explanation: "En indkomst" means "an income", the money a person or a household earns. It is the usual word in tax and official forms, where you give your årlige indkomst (yearly income).

sentence.da: Familiens samlede **indkomst** er ikke nok til at købe et hus.
sentence.en: The family's total income is not enough to buy a house.

en indkøbskurv.explanation: "En indkøbskurv" means "a shopping basket", the kind you carry by hand in a shop. A bigger one on wheels is en indkøbsvogn (a shopping cart). The word is built from indkøb (shopping) and en kurv (a basket).

sentence.da: Jeg lægger mælk og brød i min **indkøbskurv**.
sentence.en: I put milk and bread in my shopping basket.

en indkøbsliste.explanation: "En indkøbsliste" means "a shopping list", the list of things you plan to buy, on paper or in your phone. It is built from indkøb (shopping) and liste (list). Indkøb also appears in at gå på indkøb (to go shopping).

sentence.da: Jeg skriver mælk og brød på min **indkøbsliste**.
sentence.en: I write milk and bread on my shopping list.

en indkøbspose.explanation: "En indkøbspose" means "a shopping bag", a plastic or cloth bag you fill in a store. It is built from indkøb (shopping) and en pose (a bag). Pose also names a bag of food: en pose chips (a bag of chips).

sentence.da: Jeg bærer maden hjem i en **indkøbspose**.
sentence.en: I carry the food home in a shopping bag.

en indkøbstur.explanation: "En indkøbstur" means "a shopping trip", going out to buy things like groceries or clothes. You usually say at tage på indkøbstur (to go on a shopping trip).

sentence.da: Vi tager på **indkøbstur** og køber nyt tøj.
sentence.en: We go on a shopping trip and buy new clothes.

en indkøbsvogn.explanation: "En indkøbsvogn" means "a shopping cart", the kind on wheels that you push around a supermarket. It is built from indkøb (shopping) and en vogn (a cart). Vogn also appears in en barnevogn (a baby stroller).

sentence.da: Jeg skubber en **indkøbsvogn** rundt i supermarkedet.
sentence.en: I push a shopping cart around the supermarket.

en indkørsel.explanation: "En indkørsel" means "a driveway", the way from the road to a house. On a road sign, Indkørsel forbudt (No entry) means cars may not drive in.

sentence.da: Der står en bil i vores **indkørsel**.
sentence.en: There is a car standing in our driveway.

en indledning.explanation: "En indledning" means "an introduction", the first part of a text, a speech or a report, which tells what is coming. It is not for presenting a person: for that, say at præsentere (to introduce).

sentence.da: Der står en kort **indledning** først og en lang afslutning til sidst.
sentence.en: There is a short introduction first and a long conclusion at the end.

en indlæggelse.explanation: "En indlæggelse" means "a hospitalization", being admitted to a hospital to stay overnight or longer. The matching verb is at indlægge (to admit): Han er indlagt (He is admitted). A visit where you go home the same day is called ambulant (outpatient).

sentence.da: Efter operationen fik han en lang **indlæggelse** på hospitalet.
sentence.en: After the operation he had a long hospital stay.

en indlæring.explanation: "En indlæring" means "a learning process", taking in new knowledge or skills, mostly in school and studies. You often see it in compound words such as indlæringsvanskeligheder (learning difficulties).

sentence.da: Børns **indlæring** går hurtigere, når de er trygge og nysgerrige.
sentence.en: Children's learning goes faster when they feel safe and curious.

en indretning.explanation: "En indretning" means "a layout" or "furnishing", how a room or a home is arranged and decorated. It covers where things stand, not only what you buy. The matching verb is at indrette (to furnish): Vi har indrettet stuen (We have furnished the living room).

sentence.da: Lejlighedens **indretning** er enkel med hvide vægge og få møbler.
sentence.en: The apartment's furnishing is simple, with white walls and few pieces of furniture.

en indretningsarkitekt.explanation: "En indretningsarkitekt" means "an interior designer", a trained professional who plans how rooms look and are used, from colors to furniture and light. It is built from indretning (layout, furnishing) and arkitekt (architect).

sentence.da: Vi hyrer en **indretningsarkitekt**, som kan planlægge vores nye køkken.
sentence.en: We hire an interior designer who can plan our new kitchen.

en indsamling.explanation: "En indsamling" means "a collection" in the sense of gathering money or goods for a good cause. It is not a hobby collection like stamps, which is en samling (a collection). The matching verb is at samle ind (to collect money).

sentence.da: Skolen holder en **indsamling** til børn, der har mistet deres hjem.
sentence.en: The school holds a fundraiser for children who have lost their home.

en indsat.explanation: "En indsat" means "an inmate", a person who is in prison. It is the neutral word used by prison staff and in the news, and it sounds more respectful than fange (prisoner).

sentence.da: Hver **indsat** har sin egen celle i fængslet.
sentence.en: Each inmate has his own cell in the prison.

en indsats.explanation: "En indsats" means "an effort", the work and energy someone puts into something, often as a contribution to a group. Tak for din indsats (Thanks for your effort) is a common way to praise someone. It can also mean a planned action, such as a public program against a problem.

sentence.da: Takket være klassens **indsats** blev festen en stor succes.
sentence.en: Thanks to the class's effort, the party became a big success.

en indskrivning.explanation: "En indskrivning" means "an enrollment", putting a name on the list at a school or a university. Parents do it for their children before school starts: Indskrivningen begynder i januar (Enrollment begins in January).

sentence.da: Ved **indskrivning** på skolen får barnet sin plads i klassen.
sentence.en: At enrollment at the school the child gets a place in the class.

en indsprøjtning.explanation: "En indsprøjtning" means "an injection", medicine put into the body with a needle. In daily talk people often say en sprøjte (a shot): Jeg skal have en sprøjte (I am getting a shot). It is also used for money put into something, such as a company.

sentence.da: Lægen giver hende en **indsprøjtning** mod smerterne i armen.
sentence.en: The doctor gives her an injection against the pain in her arm.

en indstilling.explanation: "En indstilling" means "a setting", a choice you can adjust on a phone, a machine or a program. It has a second meaning, a person's attitude: Han har en positiv indstilling (He has a positive attitude). The context shows which one is meant.

sentence.da: Der er en **indstilling** i appen, som gør skærmen mørk.
sentence.en: There is a setting in the app that makes the screen dark.

en indtægt.explanation: "En indtægt" means "an income" or "revenue", money that comes in, for a person or a business. It is the opposite of an expense, and it often points to one source of money, such as tourists for a town.

sentence.da: Turisterne er en vigtig **indtægt** for den lille by.
sentence.en: The tourists are an important income for the small town.

en industri.explanation: "En industri" means "an industry", a branch of business that makes goods in large amounts, usually with machines: fødevareindustri (food industry), medicinalindustri (drug industry). It can also mean all such businesses of a country taken together.

sentence.da: Fabrikker og maskiner er en stor del af landets **industri**.
sentence.en: Factories and machines are a big part of the country's industry.

en indvandrer.explanation: "En indvandrer" means "an immigrant", a person who has moved to a country to live. The matching action is at indvandre (to immigrate).

sentence.da: En **indvandrer** flytter til et nyt land.
sentence.en: An immigrant moves to a new country.

en indånding.explanation: "En indånding" means "an inhalation", one drawing in of air. It is used in medical and yoga talk, often with its opposite: indånding og udånding (breathing in and out).

sentence.da: Efter en dyb **indånding** holder hun vejret i fem sekunder.
sentence.en: After a deep inhalation, she holds her breath for five seconds.

en infektion.explanation: "En infektion" means "an infection", an illness caused by germs getting into the body. Doctors often name the place, as in en halsinfektion (a throat infection). Antibiotics work on infections from bacteria, but not on those from a virus.

sentence.da: Hun har en **infektion** i øret og skal have antibiotika.
sentence.en: She has an infection in her ear and needs antibiotics.

en influencer.explanation: "En influencer" means "an influencer", the same word as in English. It is someone who shows their life online and recommends things to an audience.

sentence.da: Min søster er **influencer** og har mange følgere.
sentence.en: My sister is an influencer and has many followers.

en ingeniør.explanation: "En ingeniør" means "an engineer", someone who designs or builds technical things like machines or roads. The word is the same for men and women.

sentence.da: Min bror er **ingeniør** og bygger broer.
sentence.en: My brother is an engineer and builds bridges.

en ingrediens.explanation: "En ingrediens" means "an ingredient", one of the things a food is made from. The list on a package is en ingrediensliste (an ingredient list).

sentence.da: Vi mangler kun én **ingrediens** til kagen.
sentence.en: We are only missing one ingredient for the cake.

en innovation.explanation: "En innovation" means "an innovation", a new idea, product or method that is put to use. Unlike en opfindelse (an invention), it stresses that the new thing actually gets used.

sentence.da: En **innovation** gør det billigere at producere strøm fra vinden.
sentence.en: An innovation makes it cheaper to produce power from the wind.

en inspektør.explanation: "En inspektør" means "an inspector", a person whose job is to check that rules are followed, such as in a school, a restaurant or a factory. A fødevareinspektør (food inspector) visits shops and restaurants.

sentence.da: En **inspektør** kommer og tjekker, om restauranten holder køkkenet rent.
sentence.en: An inspector comes to check whether the restaurant keeps its kitchen clean.

en inspiration.explanation: "En inspiration" means "an inspiration", something that gives you new ideas or the wish to create. A common phrase is at hente inspiration (to get inspiration): Vi henter inspiration fra Italien (We get inspiration from Italy).

sentence.da: Naturen er en stor **inspiration** for mange malere.
sentence.en: Nature is a big inspiration for many painters.

en installation.explanation: "En installation" means "an installation", the act of fitting equipment or software so it works, or the equipment itself. In art, it is also a work built in a room. The matching verb is at installere (to install).

sentence.da: Efter en **installation** af programmet kan du bruge det med det samme.
sentence.en: After an installation of the program, you can use it right away.

en institution.explanation: "En institution" means "an institution", an organization with an important public role, such as a school, a hospital or a museum. In Denmark, a daycare for children is also called en institution, as in vuggestue (nursery) and børnehave (kindergarten).

sentence.da: Et hospital er en vigtig **institution** i et samfund.
sentence.en: A hospital is an important institution in a society.

en instruks.explanation: "En instruks" means "an instruction", written rules from an employer or an authority about exactly what to do in a certain situation, such as handling a customer complaint. It can also be an order to the person doing the job: Han handlede efter instruks (He acted on orders).

sentence.da: Personalets **instruks** siger, at man skal ringe 112 ved brand.
sentence.en: The staff's instruction says that you must call 112 in case of fire.

en instruktion.explanation: "En instruktion" means "an instruction", a piece of guidance that tells you how to do something. It is often used in the plural for a list of steps: Læs instruktionerne først (Read the instructions first). Do not mix it up with en instruktør (a director).

sentence.da: Der står en **instruktion** på pakken, som du skal følge.
sentence.en: There is an instruction on the package that you must follow.

en instruktør.explanation: "En instruktør" means "a director" of a film, play or TV show, the person who leads the cast and decides how it looks. The same word is also used for an instructor in sports: en svømmeinstruktør (a swimming instructor). Do not mix it up with en direktør (a company director).

sentence.da: Filmens **instruktør** fortæller skuespillerne, hvordan scenen skal spilles.
sentence.en: The film's director tells the actors how the scene should be played.

en integration.explanation: "En integration" means "an integration", the process of becoming a full part of a society, a school or a workplace. In Denmark it is most often used about new arrivals learning the language and finding work. It can also mean joining two computer systems.

sentence.da: Sprogkurser og arbejde hjælper med **integration** i det danske samfund.
sentence.en: Language courses and work help with integration into Danish society.

en interesse.explanation: "En interesse" means "an interest", something you like to spend time on. After interesse, the small word for links it to the topic: Han har stor interesse for biler (He has a big interest in cars). To say you are interested, use at være interesseret i (to be interested in).

sentence.da: Min store **interesse** er at male.
sentence.en: My big interest is painting.

en internetforbindelse.explanation: "En internetforbindelse" means "an internet connection", the link that lets a phone or computer get online. When the signal is gone, you can say: Jeg har ingen forbindelse (I have no connection).

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke se film uden **internetforbindelse**.
sentence.en: I cannot watch movies without an internet connection.

en invasion.explanation: "En invasion" means "an invasion", when an army enters another country by force. It is also used lightly for a big crowd arriving: en invasion af turister (an invasion of tourists).

sentence.da: Danmark blev udsat for en **invasion** i 1940.
sentence.en: Denmark was hit by an invasion in 1940.

en investering.explanation: "En investering" means "an investment", money or time you put into something to get more back later. It is used for shares and houses, and also in daily talk: Den nye cykel er en god investering (The new bike is a good investment).

sentence.da: Et hus er en stor **investering**, som du betaler af i mange år.
sentence.en: A house is a big investment that you pay off for many years.

en invitation.explanation: "En invitation" means "an invitation", a request to come to a party or event. The matching action is at invitere (to invite).

sentence.da: Jeg har fået en **invitation** til en fødselsdag.
sentence.en: I have received an invitation to a birthday party.

en irritation.explanation: "En irritation" means "an irritation", a small feeling of being bothered or upset by something. It is used for feelings and also for the body: en irritation i huden (an irritation in the skin).

sentence.da: Larmen fra naboen er en daglig **irritation** for hele familien.
sentence.en: The noise from the neighbor is a daily irritation for the whole family.

en isbjørn.explanation: "En isbjørn" means "a polar bear". It is built from is (ice) and bjørn (bear). The word is also means ice cream: Jeg vil have en is (I want an ice cream).

sentence.da: En **isbjørn** bor på isen og fanger sæler.
sentence.en: A polar bear lives on the ice and catches seals.

en isbod.explanation: "En isbod" means "an ice cream stand", a small stall that sells ice cream. Is means both "ice" and "ice cream"; bod means a small stall.

sentence.da: Vi køber en softice ved en **isbod** på stranden.
sentence.en: We buy a soft serve at an ice cream stand on the beach.

en isenkræmmer.explanation: "En isenkræmmer" means "a hardware dealer", a shopkeeper who sells everyday items for the home and workshop, called isenkram (hardware). The word sounds a bit old-fashioned today, and most people now buy such things at et byggemarked (a home improvement store).

sentence.da: En **isenkræmmer** sælger værktøj, gryder og andre ting til hjemmet.
sentence.en: A hardware dealer sells tools, pots and other things for the home.

en islænding.explanation: "En islænding" means "an Icelander", a person from Iceland. The country is Island (Iceland), and the language is islandsk (Icelandic). Do not mix it up with en irlænder (an Irishman), which looks almost the same.

sentence.da: Min ven er **islænding** og kommer fra Reykjavik.
sentence.en: My friend is an Icelander and comes from Reykjavik.

en istap.explanation: "En istap" means "an icicle", a pointed piece of ice that hangs down. It is built from is (ice) and tap (a plug or peg). The word is means both ice and ice cream: Jeg vil have en is (I want an ice cream).

sentence.da: Der hænger en lang **istap** fra taget.
sentence.en: A long icicle hangs from the roof.

en isterning.explanation: "En isterning" means "an ice cube", a small frozen block that you put in a drink. It is built from is (ice) and terning (cube). A terning is also a die for games: Slå en terning (Roll a die).

sentence.da: En **isterning** gør min drik kold.
sentence.en: An ice cube makes my drink cold.

en isvaffel.explanation: "En isvaffel" means "an ice cream cone", the crispy cone you hold ice cream in. It is built from is (ice cream) and vaffel (waffle), so it is literally an ice cream waffle. The part vaffel also stands alone: en vaffel med syltetøj (a waffle with jam).

sentence.da: Jeg får to kugler is i en **isvaffel**.
sentence.en: I get two scoops of ice cream in an ice cream cone.

en italiener.explanation: "En italiener" means "an Italian" person. For food and other things, use the matching word italiensk: italiensk mad (Italian food).

sentence.da: Min kollega er **italiener** og elsker pasta.
sentence.en: My coworker is Italian and loves pasta.

en iværksætter.explanation: "En iværksætter" means "an entrepreneur", someone who starts a new business. It comes from at iværksætte (to set going), so it carries the idea of getting something started.

sentence.da: Som **iværksætter** skal du selv finde kunder og betale dine regninger.
sentence.en: As an entrepreneur, you must find customers yourself and pay your bills.

et ildfast fad.explanation: "Et ildfast fad" means "an ovenproof dish", a dish that can take strong heat. Ildfast (fireproof) is built from ild (fire) and fast (firm). Fad alone is a serving platter: Kagen står på et fad (The cake is on a platter).

sentence.da: Jeg bager lasagnen i et **ildfast fad**.
sentence.en: I bake the lasagna in an ovenproof dish.

et imperium.explanation: "Et imperium" means "an empire", a very large power that rules over many lands and peoples. Another Danish word for the same idea is et rige (a realm), as in Romerriget (the Roman Empire).

sentence.da: Det romerske **imperium** erobrede store dele af Europa.
sentence.en: The Roman Empire conquered large parts of Europe.

et indbrud.explanation: "Et indbrud" means "a burglary", when someone breaks into a home or shop. It is built from ind (in) + brud (a break). Brud also ends et benbrud (a broken bone).

sentence.da: Ved et **indbrud** tager en tyv ting fra et hus.
sentence.en: In a burglary, a thief takes things from a house.

et indkøb.explanation: "Et indkøb" means "a purchase". It is also used for everyday shopping: Jeg skal lave indkøb (I need to do the shopping).

sentence.da: Et nyt fjernsyn er et stort **indkøb**.
sentence.en: A new TV is a big purchase.

et indkøbscenter.explanation: "Et indkøbscenter" means "a shopping mall", a large building with many shops. It is made of indkøb (shopping) and et center (a center). People also say et shoppingcenter, which means the same.

sentence.da: Der er mange butikker i et stort **indkøbscenter**.
sentence.en: There are many shops in a big shopping mall.

et indlæg.explanation: "Et indlæg" means "a post / contribution", something you add to a discussion, such as a text you publish online or a short talk in a meeting: et indlæg på Facebook (a post on Facebook). It is also the word for an insole you put in a shoe.

sentence.da: Hun skrev et langt **indlæg** i avisen om skolens fremtid.
sentence.en: She wrote a long piece in the newspaper about the future of the school.

et indtryk.explanation: "Et indtryk" means "an impression", the picture you form in your mind of someone or something after meeting or seeing it. Det gjorde stort indtryk på mig (It made a big impression on me). The opposite direction is et udtryk (an expression), what comes out.

sentence.da: Mit første **indtryk** af byen var meget godt.
sentence.en: My first impression of the city was very good.

et initiativ.explanation: "Et initiativ" means "an initiative", the first step that gets something started. Someone who starts things without being asked has initiativ. It can also be a new plan put in place by a city or a company.

sentence.da: Naboerne tog **initiativ** til en fælles have i gården.
sentence.en: The neighbors took the initiative for a shared garden in the yard.

et insekt.explanation: "Et insekt" means "an insect", a small animal with six legs. A spider is not an insect, because en edderkop (a spider) has eight legs.

sentence.da: En bi er et **insekt** med vinger.
sentence.en: A bee is an insect with wings.

et instinkt.explanation: "Et instinkt" means "an instinct", a natural urge to act in a certain way that nobody has taught you, such as a newborn animal searching for its mother's milk. You can say Jeg gjorde det af instinkt (I did it by instinct) when you acted without thinking.

sentence.da: Fuglene flyver mod syd om efteråret af **instinkt**.
sentence.en: The birds fly south in the autumn by instinct.

et institut.explanation: "Et institut" means "an institute", an organization that studies or teaches one particular subject. In higher education, a department is also called an institut. A beauty salon is et skønhedsinstitut.

sentence.da: Forskerne på et **institut** studerer ét emne meget grundigt.
sentence.en: The researchers at an institute study one topic very thoroughly.

et instrument.explanation: "Et instrument" means "an instrument", something you play music on. It is also a tool for measuring, such as et termometer (a thermometer).

sentence.da: Hun lærer et nyt **instrument**, og det er en violin.
sentence.en: She is learning a new instrument, and it is a violin.

et interview.explanation: "Et interview" means "an interview", a talk where one person asks another about their work or life. For a job interview, say en jobsamtale (a job interview).

sentence.da: Hun giver et **interview** til avisen i dag.
sentence.en: She is giving an interview to the newspaper today.

i.explanation: "I" means "in": i huset (in the house), i Danmark (in Denmark), i juni (in June). It is also used for how long something lasts: i to timer (for two hours). Compare på (on, at): på bordet (on the table), på Fyn (on Funen, an island).

sentence.da: Jeg bor **i** København.
sentence.en: I live in Copenhagen.

i aften.explanation: "I aften" means "this evening". Compare Jeg ser en film i aften (I am watching a movie this evening) with Jeg så en film i aftes (I watched a movie last night): i aften is still to come, and i aftes is over.

forms.en: What are you doing this evening?

sentence.da: Vi skal spise middag sammen **i aften**.
sentence.en: We are having dinner together this evening.

i aftes.explanation: "I aftes" means "last night", meaning the evening that just ended. Compare Jeg så en film i aftes (I watched a movie last night) with Jeg ser en film i aften (I am watching a movie this evening). For the hours when you were asleep, say i nat: Jeg sov dårligt i nat (I slept badly last night).

forms.en: I was at home last night.

sentence.da: Vi spiste pizza **i aftes**.
sentence.en: We ate pizza last night.

i dag.explanation: "I dag" means "today". For the evening of today, say i aften (this evening).

sentence.da: Jeg har fri **i dag**.
sentence.en: I am off today.

i det hele taget.explanation: "I det hele taget" means "on the whole" or "generally" and talks about things overall, not one case: Det går i det hele taget fint (It is going fine overall). In a question it can mean "at all".

forms.da: Jeg kan i det hele taget godt lide det.
Hvorfor er du her i det hele taget?
forms.en: Why are you here at all?

sentence.da: Jeg kan **i det hele taget** godt lide efteråret.
sentence.en: I generally like fall.

i det mindste.explanation: "I det mindste" means "at least" and points to the smallest good thing: Han kom i det mindste (At least he came).

sentence.da: Du kan **i det mindste** prøve det.
sentence.en: You can at least try it.

i det store hele.explanation: "I det store hele" means "all in all", a general summary that allows for small exceptions: the big picture is true even if a few details are not.

forms.da: I det store hele gik det godt
forms.en: All in all it went well

forms.da: Jeg er i det store hele enig
Det er i det store hele rigtigt
forms.en: It is by and large right

sentence.da: Vi er **i det store hele** tilfredse, men maden kunne være bedre.
sentence.en: All in all we are satisfied, but the food could be better.

i eftermiddag.explanation: "I eftermiddag" means "this afternoon", the afternoon of today. For something that happens every afternoon, say om eftermiddagen: Jeg læser om eftermiddagen (I read in the afternoons).

forms.en: What are you doing this afternoon?

sentence.da: Jeg har fri **i eftermiddag**.
sentence.en: I am off this afternoon.

i forgårs.explanation: "I forgårs" means "the day before yesterday". Count back: i dag (today), i går (yesterday), i forgårs.

forms.en: I was sick the day before yesterday.
It happened the day before yesterday.

sentence.da: Det er onsdag. **I forgårs** var det mandag.
sentence.en: It is Wednesday. The day before yesterday it was Monday.

i forhold til.explanation: "I forhold til" means "in relation to" and also "compared to": Det er billigt i forhold til Paris (It is cheap compared to Paris). It sets one thing next to another to judge it.

sentence.da: Huset er stort **i forhold til** prisen.
sentence.en: The house is big for the price.

i fortiden.explanation: "I fortiden" means "in the past", before now or long ago. For what comes later, use i fremtiden (in the future).

forms.en: In the past, people lived differently.

sentence.da: Folk skrev mange breve **i fortiden**.
sentence.en: People wrote many letters in the past.

i forvejen.explanation: "I forvejen" means "beforehand", before something happens, and also "already": Jeg kender hende i forvejen (I already know her).

sentence.da: Hun havde **i forvejen** købt billetter til os.
sentence.en: She had already bought tickets for us.

i fremtiden.explanation: "I fremtiden" means "in the future". The opposite is i fortiden (in the past).

forms.da: Jeg vil rejse mere i fremtiden.
forms.en: I want to travel more in the future.
What will happen in the future?
In the future, it will be easier.

sentence.da: Jeg vil spare flere penge **i fremtiden**.
sentence.en: I want to save more money in the future.

i første omgang.explanation: "I første omgang" means "at first", the first step of something that will go on. It often hints that more steps come later. Omgang here means a round or stage.

forms.da: Det er nok i første omgang

sentence.da: **I første omgang** skal vi bare finde et sted at bo.
sentence.en: At first, we just have to find a place to live.

i gang.explanation: "I gang" means "going" or "underway", for something that has started and is still happening. With komme (to come), it means getting started.

forms.da: Jeg er i gang med at spise
forms.en: I am in the middle of eating

sentence.da: Mødet er allerede **i gang**.
sentence.en: The meeting is already underway.

i gang med.explanation: "I gang med" means "busy with", or "in the middle of", something: Jeg er i gang med at lave mad (I am busy making food). It usually follows er (am / is / are).

forms.da: Jeg er i gang med lektierne.
forms.en: I am busy with my homework.

forms.da: Hun er i gang med at ringe.
forms.en: She is in the middle of calling.

sentence.da: Jeg er **i gang med** at læse en bog.
sentence.en: I am busy reading a book.

i går.explanation: "I går" means "yesterday". Add a time of day for more detail: i går aftes (last night) and i går morges (yesterday morning).

sentence.da: Jeg var hjemme **i går**.
sentence.en: I was at home yesterday.

i hvert fald.explanation: "I hvert fald" means "in any case" and "at least": Det er i hvert fald billigt (At least it is cheap). It points to one thing that stays true: Jeg ved ikke hvornår, men jeg kommer i hvert fald (I don't know when, but I am coming in any case).

forms.da: Jeg har i hvert fald prøvet
Det er i hvert fald godt
I hvert fald ikke i dag

sentence.da: Det regner, men det er **i hvert fald** varmt.
sentence.en: It is raining, but at least it is warm.

i kraft af.explanation: "I kraft af" means "by virtue of", and gives the reason something is allowed or possible: the power or position that comes with something. For ordinary causes such as weather, use på grund af (because of) instead.

sentence.da: Borgmesteren kan beslutte det **i kraft af** sit embede.
sentence.en: The mayor can decide it by virtue of his office.

i lige måde.explanation: "I lige måde" means "likewise" and answers a good wish by returning it. It stands in for the whole wish: after Hav en god dag! (Have a good day!) it means "you have a good day too".

sentence.da: Hav en god weekend! Tak, **i lige måde**!
sentence.en: Have a good weekend! Thanks, you too!

i mangel af.explanation: "I mangel af" means "for lack of", and it names the thing that was missing, so something else had to do. It often goes with bedre: i mangel af bedre (for lack of anything better).

sentence.da: **I mangel af** en bil gik vi hele vejen.
sentence.en: For lack of a car we walked the whole way.

i mellemtiden.explanation: "I mellemtiden" means "in the meantime" and names what happens while you wait for something else. It is built from i (in) and mellemtiden (the time between), so it points to the gap before the other thing happens.

sentence.da: Vi venter, og **i mellemtiden** drikker vi kaffe.
sentence.en: We wait, and in the meantime we drink coffee.

i modsætning til.explanation: "I modsætning til" means "in contrast to". It sets two things side by side to show that they differ: Han er rolig, i modsætning til sin søster (He is calm, unlike his sister).

sentence.da: Byen er stille om natten, **i modsætning til** om dagen.
sentence.en: The city is quiet at night, in contrast to the day.

i morgen.explanation: "I morgen" means "tomorrow". It looks like i morges (this morning, already past), so watch the last letters: i morgen is still to come, i morges is already over. Hun ringede i morges (She called this morning).

sentence.da: Jeg har fri **i morgen**.
sentence.en: I am off tomorrow.

i morges.explanation: "I morges" means "this morning", the morning of today that is already over. It looks like i morgen (tomorrow), so watch the last letters: i morges is behind you, i morgen is ahead.

forms.da: Jeg stod op tidligt i morges.
forms.en: I got up early this morning.

sentence.da: Jeg drak kaffe **i morges**.
sentence.en: I drank coffee this morning.

i nat.explanation: "I nat" means "tonight" or "last night", and the rest of the sentence shows which. Jeg sov dårligt i nat (I slept badly last night) is about the night just gone. Jeg sover hos Anna i nat (I am sleeping at Anna's tonight) is about the night to come.

sentence.da: Jeg har sovet godt **i nat**.
sentence.en: I slept well last night.

i nærheden.explanation: "I nærheden" means "nearby". Add af (of) and a place to say near that place: i nærheden af banegården (near the train station).

forms.da: Er der en butik i nærheden?

sentence.da: Er der en bank **i nærheden**?
sentence.en: Is there a bank nearby?

i og med.explanation: "I og med" means "since" or "given that". It gives a reason that is already a known fact. It is nearly always followed by at: I og med at det regner, bliver vi hjemme (Since it is raining, we stay home).

forms.da: i og med at det er søndag
i og med at han er syg
i og med at vi bor her

sentence.da: **I og med** at vi bor tæt på, cykler vi til arbejde.
sentence.en: Since we live close by, we bike to work.

i orden.explanation: "I orden" means "all right" or "in order". Det er i orden (That is all right) can answer an apology, like saying no problem. Er alt i orden? (Is everything all right?) checks that nothing is wrong.

sentence.da: Alt er **i orden**.
sentence.en: Everything is all right.

i overmorgen.explanation: "I overmorgen" means "the day after tomorrow". Count forward: i dag (today), i morgen (tomorrow), i overmorgen.

forms.en: See you the day after tomorrow.
I am leaving the day after tomorrow.

sentence.da: Vi ses **i overmorgen**.
sentence.en: See you the day after tomorrow.

i princippet.explanation: "I princippet" means "in principle" and says something is true on paper, while real life may be different. That is why a "but" often follows it.

sentence.da: **I princippet** kan alle komme, men der er kun ti pladser.
sentence.en: In principle everyone can come, but there are only ten places.

i sidste ende.explanation: "I sidste ende" means "in the end", about what counts most when everything is weighed up. It is not about time. For the last step in a series, use til sidst (at the very end).

forms.da: I sidste ende handler det om penge
forms.en: In the end, it is about money

sentence.da: **I sidste ende** er det dig, der skal vælge.
sentence.en: In the end, it is you who has to choose.

i skole.explanation: "I skole" means "in school" or "at school", as a pupil with lessons. It covers being there and heading there: Jeg skal i skole (I am off to school).

sentence.da: Børnene er **i skole** i dag.
sentence.en: The children are in school today.

i stedet.explanation: "I stedet" means "instead" and can stand alone at the end. To say instead of what, add for: Jeg vil have te i stedet for kaffe (I want tea instead of coffee).

sentence.da: Det regner, men vi går i biografen **i stedet**.
sentence.en: It is raining, but we go to the movies instead.

i stedet for.explanation: "I stedet for" means "instead of" and goes before the thing you drop. Before an action, put at (to) in front of the verb, and English uses -ing: i stedet for at vente (instead of waiting).

sentence.da: Jeg tager toget **i stedet for** bilen.
sentence.en: I take the train instead of the car.

i stykker.explanation: "I stykker" means "broken", literally in pieces, so it fits things that have fallen apart or stopped working. Use it with er (is).

sentence.da: Glasset faldt og er nu **i stykker**.
sentence.en: The glass fell and is now broken.

i tide.explanation: "I tide" means "in time", early enough for something to happen. For arriving at exactly the agreed time, say til tiden (on time): Toget kom til tiden (The train came on time).

forms.en: I made the train in time

sentence.da: Heldigvis kom jeg **i tide** til toget.
sentence.en: Luckily, I got to the train in time.

i tilfælde af.explanation: "I tilfælde af" means "in case of" and is followed by what might happen. Before a full idea, add at (that): i tilfælde af at det regner (in case it rains).

sentence.da: Ring til mig **i tilfælde af** problemer.
sentence.en: Call me in case of problems.

i udlandet.explanation: "I udlandet" means "abroad", in another country. The small word in front shows the direction: i (in) for being there, til (to) for going there, fra (from) for coming from there.

sentence.da: Min søster bor **i udlandet**.
sentence.en: My sister lives abroad.

i virkeligheden.explanation: "I virkeligheden" means "in reality" or "actually" and is used when the truth differs from how things look: Det ser nemt ud, men i virkeligheden er det svært (It looks easy, but in reality it is hard).

sentence.da: Han virker sur, men **i virkeligheden** er han meget sød.
sentence.en: He seems grumpy, but in reality he is very nice.

i weekenden.explanation: "I weekenden" means "this weekend" or "on the weekend". It can look ahead: Vi ses i weekenden (See you this weekend). It can look back: Jeg var i Aarhus i weekenden (I was in Aarhus last weekend). It also covers every weekend: Jeg sover længe i weekenden (I sleep late on weekends).

forms.en: What are you doing this weekend?

sentence.da: Jeg besøger min familie **i weekenden**.
sentence.en: I am visiting my family this weekend.

i år.explanation: "I år" means "this year": Det er varmt i år (It is warm this year). It is different from hvert år (every year): Vi rejser hvert år (We travel every year) repeats, while i år is only the current year.

sentence.da: Vi skal på ferie **i år**.
sentence.en: We are going on vacation this year.

i øvrigt.explanation: "I øvrigt" means "by the way" and "moreover". It adds a side remark or one more point to what was already said, not the main message, and it sits inside the sentence, usually right after the verb.

forms.en: By the way, he is Danish
That is also true, by the way

sentence.da: Han er **i øvrigt** min bror.
sentence.en: By the way, he is my brother.

iblandt.explanation: "Iblandt" means "among", inside a group: Han var iblandt de bedste (He was among the best). Blandt is the shorter form and is more common.

sentence.da: Min onkel er **iblandt** gæsterne til festen.
sentence.en: My uncle is among the guests at the party.

ideel.explanation: "Ideel" means "ideal", the best possible for a certain purpose. The thing you aim for is et ideal (an ideal).

sentence.da: En indhegnet have er en **ideel** legeplads for små børn.
sentence.en: A fenced garden is an ideal playground for small children.

identisk.explanation: "Identisk" means "identical", exactly the same in every detail. It is followed by med for what it matches: Svaret er identisk med mit (The answer is identical to mine).

sentence.da: Hans kopi af nøglen er **identisk** med originalen.
sentence.en: His copy of the key is identical to the original.

idet.explanation: "Idet" means "as", for two things that happen at the same moment: Idet han gik ud, slukkede han lyset (As he went out, he turned off the light). It can also give a reason, like "since": Idet det regner, aflyser vi (Since it is raining, we cancel).

sentence.da: Han smilede, **idet** han åbnede døren.
sentence.en: He smiled as he opened the door.

idræt.explanation: "Idræt" means "PE" or "sports". At school it is the gym class: Vi har idræt efter frokost (We have PE after lunch). Outside school it means sports in general: Hun elsker idræt (She loves sports).

sentence.da: Vi løber og spiller bold i **idræt**.
sentence.en: We run and play ball in PE.

ifølge.explanation: "Ifølge" means "according to". It is followed by where the information comes from: ifølge lægen (according to the doctor). For your own view, say efter min mening (in my opinion).

sentence.da: **Ifølge** vejrudsigten bliver det koldt i morgen.
sentence.en: According to the weather forecast, it will be cold tomorrow.

igen.explanation: "Igen" means "again". Compare Jeg kommer igen (I will come again, or come back) with Jeg kommer også (I am coming too). Igen repeats something, while også adds one more person or thing.

sentence.da: Kan du sige det **igen**?
sentence.en: Can you say that again?

igennem.explanation: "Igennem" means "through", going from one side of something to the other. After a verb it can also mean "from start to finish", as in reading or checking something completely.

sentence.da: Vi går **igennem** parken.
sentence.en: We walk through the park.

ikke.explanation: "Ikke" means "not" and goes right after words like er (is) and kan (can). It is not the answer no: that is nej, as in Nej, jeg er ikke sulten (No, I am not hungry). Before a thing you do not have, Danish often uses ingen (no): Jeg har ingen penge (I have no money).

sentence.da: Jeg er **ikke** sulten.
sentence.en: I am not hungry.

ikke desto mindre.explanation: "Ikke desto mindre" means "nevertheless". It points to something that is still true despite what was just said: Det var dyrt. Ikke desto mindre købte vi det (It was expensive. Nevertheless, we bought it). In everyday speech, alligevel (anyway) is more common.

sentence.da: Det regnede, men vi gik **ikke desto mindre** en tur.
sentence.en: It rained, but we went for a walk nevertheless.

ikke endnu.explanation: "Ikke endnu" means "not yet" and answers a question like Are you ready? In a longer sentence endnu usually goes last: Jeg har ikke spist endnu (I have not eaten yet). Compare ikke mere (not anymore): Jeg spiser ikke mere (I am not eating anymore).

sentence.da: Har du spist? – **Ikke endnu**.
sentence.en: Have you eaten? – Not yet.

ikke engang.explanation: "Ikke engang" means "not even" and shows that something is surprising: the thing named is the one you would least expect to be missing. It goes right before that thing.

forms.en: He did not even say thanks.

sentence.da: Han har **ikke engang** en telefon.
sentence.en: He does not even have a phone.

ikke mere.explanation: "Ikke mere" means no more (you have had enough) or not anymore (something has stopped). Ikke mere, tak (No more, thank you) is a polite way to refuse more food or drink.

sentence.da: Jeg vil **ikke mere**, tak.
sentence.en: I don't want any more, thank you.

ild.explanation: "Ild" means "fire" as in flames. Do not mix it up with en brand (a fire that does damage) or et bål (a campfire). Der er ild i huset (The house is on fire).

sentence.da: Vi fryser og tænder en **ild**.
sentence.en: We are freezing and light a fire.

ilt.explanation: "Ilt" means "oxygen", the part of the air that people and animals need in order to live. Fish take ilt from the water too: Fisk tager ilt fra vandet (Fish take oxygen from the water).

sentence.da: Bjergbestigere har brug for ekstra **ilt** højt oppe i bjergene.
sentence.en: Mountain climbers need extra oxygen high up in the mountains.

imellem.explanation: "Imellem" means "between". In the phrase en gang imellem it means "once in a while". The shorter mellem (between) means the same and is more common.

sentence.da: Jeg sidder **imellem** Anna og Peter.
sentence.en: I am sitting between Anna and Peter.

imens.explanation: "Imens" means "meanwhile" and also "while". As "while" it joins two things happening together; as "meanwhile" it can stand on its own, even at the end of a sentence.

forms.da: Du læser, imens jeg laver mad

sentence.da: Jeg laver mad, **imens** du dækker bord.
sentence.en: I cook while you set the table.

immunitet.explanation: "En immunitet" means "immunity", the body's protection against a disease: Hun har immunitet mod influenza (She has immunity to the flu). It also means legal protection: diplomatisk immunitet (diplomatic immunity).

sentence.da: Efter vaccinen har børnene **immunitet** mod mæslinger.
sentence.en: After the vaccine, the children have immunity to measles.

imod.explanation: "Imod" means "against": Vi spiller imod dem (We play against them). It also means "toward": Hun gik imod døren (She walked toward the door).

sentence.da: Jeg er **imod** den idé.
sentence.en: I am against that idea.

imponerende.explanation: "Imponerende" means "impressive", for something that makes people admire the skill or effort behind it. The person who feels it is imponeret (impressed).

sentence.da: Du løb et maraton? Det er **imponerende**!
sentence.en: You ran a marathon? That is impressive!

imponeret.explanation: "Imponeret" means "impressed". Use over for what impressed you: Jeg er meget imponeret over resultatet (I am very impressed with the result).

sentence.da: Læreren var **imponeret** over hendes arbejde.
sentence.en: The teacher was impressed by her work.

import.explanation: "En import" means "import", goods that are bought abroad and brought into a country: Importen af kaffe stiger (The import of coffee is rising). The opposite is eksport (export).

sentence.da: Danmark har stor **import** af frugt fra varme lande.
sentence.en: Denmark has large imports of fruit from warm countries.

impulsiv.explanation: "Impulsiv" means "impulsive", acting on a sudden urge without thinking first. The urge is en impuls (an impulse), and et impulskøb is something you buy on impulse.

sentence.da: Han er **impulsiv** og køber ting uden at tænke over det.
sentence.en: He is impulsive and buys things without thinking about it.

ind.explanation: "Ind" means "in". Compare Kom ind! (Come in! — you are outside and move inside) with Han er inde (He is inside — he is already there). Ind i means "into": Hun løber ind i butikken (She runs into the shop).

sentence.da: Kom **ind** i huset!
sentence.en: Come into the house!

indadvendt.explanation: "Indadvendt" means "introverted", someone who keeps to themselves and needs time alone. It is built from indad (inward) and vendt (turned), so it means "turned inward". The opposite is udadvendt (extroverted).

sentence.da: Hun er **indadvendt** og bliver hellere hjemme end at gå til fest.
sentence.en: She is introverted and would rather stay home than go to a party.

indbydende.explanation: "Indbydende" means "inviting", something that looks so pleasant that you want to come in or try it. It is often said about rooms, food and water: Vandet så indbydende ud (The water looked inviting).

sentence.da: Den nybagte kage på bordet ser **indbydende** ud.
sentence.en: The freshly baked cake on the table looks inviting.

indefra.explanation: "Indefra" means "from the inside", when something comes from or is done within the place you are talking about. The opposite is udefra (from the outside).

sentence.da: Vi kunne høre musik **indefra**.
sentence.en: We could hear music from inside.

inden.explanation: "Inden" means "before" and links an action to one that comes after it. Inden for means "within", for a time limit.

sentence.da: Ring til mig **inden** du kommer.
sentence.en: Call me before you come.

indenfor.explanation: "Indenfor" means "inside". You say it at the door to invite someone in: Kom indenfor! (Come in!). With a time it means "within": indenfor en uge (within a week).

sentence.da: Kom **indenfor** i huset!
sentence.en: Come inside the house!

indeni.explanation: "Indeni" means "inside" and tells what is inside something: Æblet er råddent indeni (The apple is rotten inside). It can also be about feelings: Jeg er glad indeni (I am happy inside).

sentence.da: Kassen ser tom ud, men der er noget **indeni**.
sentence.en: The box looks empty, but there is something inside.

indenlandsk.explanation: "Indenlandsk" means "domestic", something that stays within one country, such as flights, goods and sales. For flights, Danes also say indenrigsflyvning (domestic flight).

sentence.da: Det er en **indenlandsk** flyvning fra København til Aalborg.
sentence.en: It is a domestic flight from Copenhagen to Aalborg.

inderst.explanation: "Inderst" means "innermost", the place furthest in. In the set phrase inderst inde it means "deep down" and is about true feelings people may hide: Inderst inde er han bange (Deep down he is afraid).

forms.en: at the very back of the closet

sentence.da: Passet ligger **inderst** i skuffen, bag alle papirerne.
sentence.en: The passport is at the very back of the drawer, behind all the papers.

indflydelsesrig.explanation: "Indflydelsesrig" means "influential", having the power to change what others think or decide. It is built from en indflydelse (influence) and rig (rich), so it means "rich in influence". The phrase at have indflydelse på means "to have influence on".

sentence.da: Hun er en **indflydelsesrig** leder, og alle lytter til hende.
sentence.en: She is an influential leader, and everyone listens to her.

indfødsret.explanation: "En indfødsret" means "a citizenship", the legal right to belong to a country as one of its own people. It is the formal word in law and news; in everyday talk people say statsborgerskab (citizenship).

sentence.da: Man skal bo i landet i mange år for at få **indfødsret**.
sentence.en: You have to live in the country for many years to get citizenship.

indfødt.explanation: "Indfødt" means "native", for a person born in a given place: en indfødt københavner (a native Copenhagener). It is about where someone was born, not where they live now.

sentence.da: Hun er **indfødt** dansker og har boet her hele livet.
sentence.en: She is a native Dane and has lived here her whole life.

indhold.explanation: "Et indhold" means "content", what something holds, like the things in a box or the information in a text: indholdet i flasken (the content of the bottle).

sentence.da: Alt **indhold** på siden er gratis at læse.
sentence.en: All content on the page is free to read.

indien.explanation: "Indien" means "India". A person from India is en inder (an Indian); do not mix it up with en indianer (a Native American).

sentence.da: **Indien** er et stort land.
sentence.en: India is a big country.

indimellem.explanation: "Indimellem" means "now and then", for things that happen from time to time but not on a fixed schedule: Vi spiser ude indimellem (We eat out now and then).

forms.en: We see each other now and then

sentence.da: Jeg tager **indimellem** på café, når jeg har fri.
sentence.en: I go to a cafe now and then when I am off.

indisk.explanation: "Indisk" means "Indian", from India (Indien). It is written with a small letter (indisk), while English Indian has a capital letter. Do not mix it up with indianer (a Native American).

sentence.da: Jeg spiser gerne **indisk** mad.
sentence.en: I like eating Indian food.

individuel.explanation: "Individuel" means "individual", made for or about one person instead of a group. A person seen on their own is et individ (an individual).

sentence.da: Læreren laver en **individuel** plan til hver elev.
sentence.en: The teacher makes an individual plan for each student.

indlysende.explanation: "Indlysende" means "obvious", so clear that no explanation is needed: Det er indlysende, at han har ret (It is obvious that he is right). The opposite is uklar (unclear).

sentence.da: Svaret er **indlysende**, når man kigger på tallene.
sentence.en: The answer is obvious when you look at the numbers.

indre.explanation: "Indre" means "inner", for what is on the inside: den indre by (the inner city). It also fits feelings: indre uro (inner unrest).

sentence.da: Jeg finder **indre** ro i naturen.
sentence.en: I find inner peace in nature.

indsigt.explanation: "En indsigt" means "insight", a deeper grasp of something. It is often used with i: Hun har god indsigt i økonomi (She has good insight into economics).

sentence.da: Bogen giver os **indsigt** i, hvordan hjernen virker.
sentence.en: The book gives us insight into how the brain works.

indtil.explanation: "Indtil" means "until" and works before a time or before a full idea: Bliv, indtil du er rask (Stay until you are well). Indtil videre means "for now".

sentence.da: Vi venter **indtil** klokken seks.
sentence.en: We wait until six o'clock.

indtil nu.explanation: "Indtil nu" means "until now" and looks back at how things have been. To look ahead, use fra nu af (from now on).

forms.da: Indtil nu har det været godt.
forms.en: Until now it has been good.

forms.da: Indtil nu har jeg ikke set filmen.
forms.en: Until now I have not seen the film.

forms.da: Indtil nu er vi ikke kommet for sent.
forms.en: Until now we haven't been late.

sentence.da: Det har været en god dag **indtil nu**.
sentence.en: It has been a good day until now.

indtil videre.explanation: "Indtil videre" means "for now" or "so far", until something changes. It looks forward as "for now" and backward as "so far", and the rest of the sentence shows which.

forms.en: It is going well so far.
We are staying here for now.

sentence.da: Vi bor i en lille lejlighed **indtil videre**.
sentence.en: We live in a small apartment for now.

indviklet.explanation: "Indviklet" means "complicated", with so many parts or steps that it is hard to follow. It comes from at indvikle (to wrap up or tangle), so something indviklet is tangled.

sentence.da: Spillet er **indviklet** og svært at lære.
sentence.en: The game is complicated and hard to learn.

ineffektiv.explanation: "Ineffektiv" means "inefficient", doing something in a way that wastes time or effort. It can also mean that something does not give the result you want: en ineffektiv medicin (a medicine that does not work well).

sentence.da: Metoden er **ineffektiv**, fordi den tager alt for lang tid.
sentence.en: The method is inefficient because it takes far too long.

inficeret.explanation: "Inficeret" means "infected", reached by germs, as in a wound. Computers can be inficeret too, by a harmful program. For a person with an illness, Danes usually say smittet: Han er smittet (He is infected).

sentence.da: Såret blev **inficeret**, fordi vi ikke rensede det.
sentence.en: The wound became infected because we did not clean it.

inflation.explanation: "En inflation" means "inflation", a general rise in prices over time, so the same money buys less: Inflationen er på to procent (Inflation is at two percent).

sentence.da: Med høj **inflation** kan man købe mindre for de samme penge.
sentence.en: With high inflation, you can buy less for the same money.

influenza.explanation: "Influenza" means "flu". Danes say Jeg har influenza (I have the flu) without en (a) in front.

sentence.da: Jeg har **influenza** og skal blive hjemme.
sentence.en: I have the flu and have to stay home.

information.explanation: "Information" means "information", facts that tell you about something, such as a place, a time or a price. It is spelled like the English word, so you can recognize it in writing.

sentence.da: Turistkontoret giver **information** om byen.
sentence.en: The tourist office gives information about the city.

informeret.explanation: "Informeret" means "informed", knowing the facts you need before you decide or act. The topic comes after om: Er du informeret om ændringen? (Are you informed about the change?)

sentence.da: Før valget vil jeg gerne være godt **informeret**.
sentence.en: Before the election, I want to be well informed.

ingefær.explanation: "Ingefær" means "ginger", the sharp, warm root used to flavor food and drinks.

sentence.da: Jeg laver te med frisk **ingefær**.
sentence.en: I make tea with fresh ginger.
